metadata.disclaimer: Mappings describe capability equivalence, not operational equivalence. Verify against current provider documentation. Cost figures are indicative ranges from pricing assumptions, not quotes. The draft spec requires human review.

summary.portability_method: percentage of complexity-weighted resources (low=1, medium=2, high=3) whose mapping is equivalent/compatible and within the Hermes v1alpha1 provisioning scope (hermes_support: implemented)

data_volume.basis: inventory size_bytes: S3 from CloudWatch daily storage metrics, RDS/EBS provisioned storage (upper bound), DynamoDB table size

transfer_cost.method: low = required data (1953.6 GB) x cheapest listed AWS internet egress rate (aws-internet-egress-tier4); high = required+optional data (1953.6 GB) x (highest AWS egress rate (aws-internet-egress-tier1) + highest gcp transfer/replication fee). Free allowances, request charges and dual-running costs are not modelled.

rates_used.applies_to: Data transfer out to the internet, above 150 TB/month; US and most EU regions [S]
Data transfer out to the internet, first 10 TB/month after the 100 GB/month free allowance; US and most EU regions [S]
As above, within APAC, per GiB (an April 2025 report listed 0.09) [S]

exit_programmes: May apply (not subtracted): Transfer cost range (designed for hermes migrate assess): low = cheapest viable path (for GCP, the managed-private-network rate for the region when the S3 region is supported; otherwise tiered AWS egress), high = tiered AWS internet egress with no waiver. Report the rate ids used.

May apply (not subtracted): Exit programme, AWS: free data transfer out to the internet for customers moving off AWS may apply; it requires a request to and approval by AWS Support before the move, covers moving all data (from all eligible accounts, or all data of a particular service), and must complete within a window (180 days for non-EU customers per the 2026-10-08 update; EU customers follow the AWS EU Data Act addendum). Earlier coverage listed CloudFront, Direct Connect, Snow Family and Global Accelerator transfers as excluded. Verify current terms: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/free-data-transfer-out-to-internet-when-moving-out-of-aws/ [V for the blog terms, S for exclusions].

May apply (not subtracted): Exit programme, GCP (relevant only when leaving GCP, for example a rollback after cutover): free data transfer for customers exiting Google Cloud may apply; it requires an Exit Notice before the agreement ends, migration within an initiation period, a Completion Notice and a full exit of the service; credit appears on the final invoice; internet transfers only. Verify: https://cloud.google.com/exit-cloud [S].

May apply (not subtracted): Multicloud, GCP (EU and UK): Data Transfer Essentials (2025-09-10) may zero-rate qualifying egress between GCP and another provider for workloads of one organization running in parallel; opt-in, and traffic must be designated. Useful during coexistence, not for a one-time exit. Verify: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/networking/new-for-the-uk-and-eu-no-cost-multicloud-data-transfer-essentials [S].

May apply (not subtracted): Exit programme, Alibaba Cloud: no exit or switching waiver programme was found in this review [U]. The EU Data Act bans switching charges, including egress for switching, from 2027-01-12; it may apply to EU customers of any provider; verify with the provider [S].
